Definition: from G970; to force, i.e. (reflexively) to crowd oneself (into), or (passively) to be seized:--press, suffer violence.
BiblicalUsage: To force one's way in is the word for pressing, crowding, seizing — and it appears twice, both times about the kingdom. In Matthew 11:12 Jesus says the kingdom suffereth violence, and in Luke 16:16 he says every man presseth into it since the days of John. The same pressing, from two Gospels.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the pressing is the point: the kingdom is not entered by drifting, but by people who mean to get in.
